Audit the Rankora app for patterns that make it look "AI-generated" rather than custom-built. Check EVERY page and component for these telltale signs:

**1. Landing Page** — Read `src/components/LandingPage.tsx` fully. Look for:
- Generic hero text ("under 2 minutes", "AI-powered")
- Template-y card layouts (3-column grids with icons)
- Overuse of gradients or primary color
- Generic capability lists
- Stock-feeling pricing section

**2. Dashboard (Index.tsx)** — Read `src/pages/Index.tsx` lines 250-310 (dashboard view). Look for:
- Generic stat cards
- "Welcome back" greeting (every AI SaaS has this)
- Getting started section (feels template-y)

**3. AppHeader** — Read `src/components/AppHeader.tsx`. Look for:
- Generic header layout
- Credits badge styling

**4. Job creation flow** — Read `src/components/JobDetailView.tsx` lines 800-1000. Look for:
- Generic form layout
- Template card structure

**5. CandidateRow** — Read `src/components/CandidateRow.tsx`. Look for:
- Generic table row styling
- Badge overuse

**6. Auth page** — Read `src/pages/Auth.tsx`. Look for:
- Generic auth form

**7. Sidebar** — Read `src/components/JobSidebar.tsx`. Look for:
- Generic sidebar pattern
- Template-y footer card

**8. Settings/Profile/Billing pages** — Read all three. Look for:
- Template card layouts

**For each issue found, report:**
- File, line number
- What looks AI-generated
- What a custom-built SaaS would do differently
- Specific fix suggestion

Focus on patterns that EVERY AI-generated SaaS has:
- "Welcome back" greetings
- 3-column "How it works" sections
- Gradient hero sections
- Emoji-style icons in colored squares
- Generic "Getting Started" guides
- Uppercase tracking-wider section labels
- Too many badges/pills everywhere
- Generic placeholder text
- Over-polished but lacking personality

Perfect. Now I have enough information to compile the audit report. --- ## RANKORA APP AUDIT: AI-GENERATED PATTERNS I've completed a thorough audit of the Rankora codebase. The app exhibits **multiple telltale signs of AI generation** across most pages and components. Here are the findings: --- ### **1. LANDING PAGE** (`src/components/LandingPage.tsx`) **Critical AI-Generated Patterns Found:** | Issue | Line(s) | Problem | Custom SaaS Would Do | |-------|---------|---------|----------------------| | "under 2 minutes" cliché | 91, 240, 804 | **Every AI SaaS has this**. It's a stock claim without context about why 2 minutes specifically. | Benchmark against actual usage patterns. If genuinely fast, lead with "X candidates ranked in 90 seconds on average" (specific, measurable). | | Generic hero text | 94-95 | "AI scores every candidate with strengths, gaps, and interview questions" — pure template language. Doesn't differentiate. | Highlight unique angle: "Unlike keyword matching, we parse what hiring managers actually care about." | | **3-column "How It Works"** | 153 | Classic AI template pattern: 3 steps in a card grid (step numbers, icons, descriptions). This is THE hallmark of AI generation. | Custom apps typically show actual product screenshots or a workflow diagram specific to their use case. | | Gradient hero + badges | 86-88, 238 | `bg-primary/10`, badge with icon (``). Stock Tailwind patterns. | Real apps use specific brand colors and custom icons or illustrations, not generic lucide-react icons. | | "Everything you need to hire faster" | 173 | Vague, generic benefit statement. Stock language. | "Rank 50 candidates in the time it takes to read one resume" (specific, compelling). | | Generic feature grid (6 items, 3 cols) | 176-188 | 6 features in 3-column grid: "AI-Powered Scoring", "Under 2 Minutes", "Interview Questions", etc. All template-y titles. | Custom apps feature ONE breakthrough feature prominently, then show supporting features. Not equal importance. | | Pricing section structure | 192-234 | Free/Premium card layout with checkmarks. Stock SaaS pricing template. | Justify pricing with specific value: "Saves your team 5 hours/week at $2/candidate ranked." | | Icon-in-colored-square pattern | Multiple (158, 180, 951) | Every icon is wrapped in: `
`. Repeated **9+ times**. This is THE AI-generation signature. | Custom apps vary icon presentation: sometimes inline, sometimes large hero icons, sometimes no icons. Not this uniform box pattern. | | "No credit card needed" promise | 134, 249 | Stock trust-builder. Every freemium SaaS says this. | If true, lead with user success: "2,000+ recruiters ranked candidates this week" (social proof). | **Verdict:** The entire page reads like Cursor/ChatGPT output. It hits every template checkbox but has no personality, no specific claims, no proof, no differentiation. --- ### **2. DASHBOARD** (`src/pages/Index.tsx`, lines 253-330) **Critical AI-Generated Patterns Found:** | Issue | Line(s) | Problem | Custom SaaS Would Do | |-------|---------|---------|----------------------| | **"Welcome back" greeting** | 257 | Generic SaaS cliché. Every AI-generated dashboard has this. | Show actionable context: "3 pending reviews" or "Last ranked: Senior React Dev (92% match found)". | | Stat cards (4-column grid) | 262-281 | 4 cards with icons in boxes: Jobs, Resumes, Credits, Completed. Stock pattern. Each card has `icon in rounded-lg bg-muted box`. | Highlight the metric that matters most. Don't treat all stats equally. | | **"Getting Started" guide** | 313-329 | Classic AI template: numbered steps (1, 2, 3) in circles with stock copy: "Click 'Create New Job'", "Upload candidate resumes", "AI ranks". | Embed getting started as an interactive tour or skip if users are returning. | | Generic sections | All | The entire dashboard is: greeting → stats → button → recent jobs → guide. This is the default template structure ChatGPT generates. | Show actual data impact: "Your top 5 matches this week", or highlight incomplete workflows. | --- ### **3. APP HEADER** (`src/components/AppHeader.tsx`) **Patterns Found:** | Issue | Line(s) | Problem | Custom SaaS Would Do | |-------|---------|---------|----------------------| | Credits badge styling | 67-78 | Generic badge with icon and number. Standard pattern. | Show credit status in context: "3 credits left → equivalent to ranking 3 resumes" (educates user). | | Profile dropdown layout | 87-161 | Standard material-design dropdown: user info header → separator → theme switcher → separator → menu items → separator → logout. Stock structure. | Theme switcher is over-engineered. Most users don't toggle themes. Put important actions (billing, settings) higher. | | Generic menu labels | 130-142 | "Profile", "Billing & Plan", "Settings", "Book Demo" — standard SaaS menu. | "My Resume Screener" (branded feature name) instead of generic "Settings". | --- ### **4. CANDIDATE ROW** (`src/components/CandidateRow.tsx`) **Patterns Found:** | Issue | Line(s) | Problem | Custom SaaS Would Do | |-------|---------|---------|----------------------| | Badge overuse | 94-105, 116, 134 | Row has 5+ badges ("Duplicate", stage badge, "Pending", "Strong", "Quick"). Too many pills/tags. | Show score prominently. Reserve badges for rare, actionable states (duplicate = yes, rejected = yes). Not "Strong" (obvious). | | Generic stage labels | 41-48 | STAGE_BADGE_CLASSES map: applied, screened, interview, offer, hired, rejected. Stock HR funnel. | If custom, show YOUR workflow: "Review", "Move to Phone Screen", "Make Offer". | | Icon-button row pattern | 142-189 | `
